cbd.def: The central business district: the commercial core of a city, with offices, stores and the highest land values.

concentric-zone-model.def: Burgess's 1925 model, based on Chicago, in which a city grows outward in rings around the CBD, from a zone in transition to a commuter zone.

sector-model.def: Hoyt's 1939 model in which land uses form wedges that spread outward from the CBD along transport lines, with high-rent wedges continuing in one direction.

multiple-nuclei-model.def: Harris and Ullman's 1945 model in which a city has several centers, such as a CBD, a port, a university and an industrial district, each drawing its own land uses.

galactic-city-model.def: A model of car-based US metro areas in which an old downtown is ringed by suburbs and edge cities spaced along a beltway; also called the peripheral model.

latin-american-city-model.def: A model of Latin American cities with a CBD by the main plaza, a wealthy commercial spine, rings that get poorer outward and squatter settlements at the edge.

southeast-asian-city-model.def: A model of Southeast Asian cities centered on the old colonial port, with commercial, government and mixed zones, new suburbs and market gardens at the edge.

african-city-model.def: A model of African cities with three CBDs (colonial, traditional and market), ethnic neighborhoods, a mining or factory zone and informal settlements at the edge.

squatter-settlement.def: Housing built by residents on land they do not legally own or rent, often lacking piped water, sewers and secure title; also called an informal settlement.
